Hi There! You weren't supposed to find this yet, so congratulations on searching me up and looking through my github!

The purpose of this website is to provide a nice place for people to see what I am working on, whether they be collaborators (current and former) or recruiters. I am also using this as an opportunity to stay on top of the current trends in data science, here to record what I have been working on and learning so that I can be a better analyst.

Currently I am still editing and learning the ropes, so while you are free to browse keep in mind I do not intend for this website to be public and given out to recruiters yet.

Thanks for visiting!

# For Recruiters:

## About Me

I am a data scientist with a background in Astrophysics research, I have been working with big data for the past 4 years. I got my B.S. in Astrophysics from the University of Minnesota in 2021. I then took a year gap year working as a researcher under Prof. Claudia Scarlata. This work led me to apply to graduate school, where I ended up attending the University of Minnesota for a Masters of Science in Astrophysics, which I received at the beginning of 2025. Much of my research has been in extragalactic evolution, with an emphasis on studying star-formation rates in galaxies. Due to my affiliation with the Euclid Space Telescope I also dedicated much of my time in my masters program to working with the Euclid data pipeline, working in structure (SQL) and unstructured (DBview) databases. This work led to multiple contributions to the Euclid collaboration, mostly in the form of data validation and the creation of python-based data pipelines that enabled scientists to access Euclid data before their scheduled releases.

My education and research have led me to develop a wide array of tools well befitting that of a data scientist, from modern AI and machine learning to classics like MCMC and regression. Astrophysics has been the birthplace of many modern statistical and computational techniques, and has uniquely prepared me to embrace the ever-changing landscape of data science.

# For Everyone Else:

Hello! I find it strange you are here, but happy you made it. This website has two main functions. The first is to provide deeper insight for recruiters as to who I am and what I am currently up to. The other is to provide a nice public space for me to share what I have been up to. This is primarily in the lens of learning new data science techniques, as well as keeping up any of my Astrophysics research, as while I have left the field professionally I still maintain a passion for it in my heart. Ideally, as I continue working on things and learning new things, this website will be a place for others to learn the same techniques.

Thanks for stopping by, and I hope you have a wonderful day.
